entities.summary: Mamercus Aemilius Lepidus Livianus was a Roman politician and military commander who played a crucial role in the Roman Republic's transition to the Imperial era. He served as consul in 77 BC, a period marked by significant political and social upheaval in Rome. The fall of the Roman Republic and the rise of the Roman Empire were influenced by the actions of Lepidus and other prominent Roman leaders. The consequences of Lepidus' actions were far-reaching, with the Roman Empire's expansion and the eventual division of the empire into Eastern and Western halves being shaped by his decisions. The legacy of Lepidus can be seen in the continued influence of the Roman Empire on modern Western society and politics. In the annals of Roman history, Lepidus' name stands as a testament to the enduring power of Roman politics and the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the Roman Republic's final decades.
